                                      INTRODUCTION

Q. Please state your name and address.

A. My name is Ryan Hopkins. My business address is 2923 CR 202, Burnet, TX 78611.


Q. Can you remind the Judges of your business?

A. Yes, I own and operate my business, Lone Star Land Protection (LSLP). LSLP

provides Iandowner-side consulting for Texans affected by energy utility mineral, and

infrastructure projects.

Q. Have you been tendered as an expert witness in this matter?

A. Yes, I was tendered as an expert witness by G6 Landowners Legal Fund, LLC, and

no party filed objections to my testifying as an expert witness.

             PURPOSE AND BASIS OF CROSS-REBUTTAL TESTIMONY

Q. What are the purposes of your cross-rebuttal testimony in this proceeding?

A. Parties in this proceeding filed direct testimony through which witnesses proposed

alternative routes that included the G6 link. I have reviewed and analyzed that testimony

and the exhibits or attachments used to support that testimony The purpose of my

cross-rebuttal testimony is to provide the Administrative Law Judges and the Public

Utility Commission of Texas ("Commission") the results of my analysis considering the

statutory and regulatory factors that the Commission is required to consider under

PURA § 37.056(c) and 16 TAC § 25.101(b)(3)(B); and applying those factors specifically



                                                      Cross-Rebuttal Testimony of Ryan Hopkins
                                                 on Behalf of the G6 Landowners Legal Fund LLC
                                                    regarding Brewer and Smitherman Testimony
                                                                  on behalf of Save the Lampasas
                                                                          PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                  SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                      Page 4 of 38
 to the alternative routes that included the G6 link that were proposed in direct testimony

on behalf of other parties in this proceeding.

Q. Were your cross-rebuttal testimony and related attachments prepared by you

or under your supervision?

A. Yes.

Q. Are your cross-rebuttal testimony and related attachments true and correct to

the best of your knowledge and belief?

A. Yes.

Q. What is the basis for your cross-rebuttal testimony in this proceeding?

A. My testimony is based on my expert opinions, which are within my areas of

expertise: transmission line right-of-way acquisition, transmission line siting, parcel-level

constraints analysis, and the statutory and regulatory framework that governs CCN

proceedings for high-voltage transmission lines under PURA § 37.056 and 16 TAC §

25.101. In addition, for this cross-rebuttal I have conducted an independent multi-route

composite scoring analysis of 123 routes, the 122 routes filed with the Application and

the additional route proposed by Ms. Reinecke on behalf of Cherokee Creek Partners,

using data sourced entirely from the Applicants' own filed materials. That analysis is

described in detail in the Affirmative Route Analysis section of this testimony.

 Q. What materials have you reviewed in the preparation of your cross-rebuttal for

this proceeding?

A. I have reviewed:


       (1) the Application filed by Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC and LCRA

Transmission Service Corporation in this docket, including the route-tier shape files and

constraint disclosures for the G6 Link;

       (2) the direct testimony of Rae Lynn Schneider Reinecke - President/Owner,

Integrated Environmental Solutions, LLC (IES), McKinney TX on behalf of Cherokee

Creek Partners; Bonnie Helene McAnelly (individually and as Trustee of the 2025

Homestead Trust and the Bonnie Helene McAnelly 2023 Trust (collectively referred

herein as "CCP") (Interchange Filing No. 4204);

       (3) the direct testimony of Aaron Brewer, P. G., Managing Director, Natural

Resources, ESE Partners (Austin, TX) (Interchange Filing No. 4494) and Barry T.

Smitherman on behalf of Save The Lampasas, Carpenter Land & Cattle, Martin, and the

N3 Opposition Landowner Group (collectively referred herein as "STL")(Interchange

Filing No. 4339); and


       (4) Applicants' Response to CCP's Request for Information regarding alternative

routes requested by CCP, including Route CCG (Interchange Filing No. 3787).

I have reviewed and analyzed the testimony of the listed witnesses and the exhibits or

attachments used to support that testimony and applied the statutory and regulatory

 factors that the Commission is required to consider under PURA § 37.056(c) and 16

TAC § 25.101(b)(3)(B) to prepare the opinions I present in this cross-rebuttal testimony.

I have also conducted an independent composite scoring analysis of all 123 routes

using the Applicants' own filed data, described in detail below.


                                SUMMARY OF OPINIONS

Q. Based upon your understanding of the Application; your education,

experience, and expertise; and your review of the testimony you have just listed

and the exhibits or attachments used to support that testimony, have you formed

opinions as to issues relevant to the criteria required for Commission approval in

PURA § 37.056(c)(4); 16 TAC § 25.101(b)(3)(B)?


A. Yes, I have.


Q. In your expert opinion, did you identify flaws or omissions in the analysis

provided by Mr. Brewer in his direct testimony that are relevant to the criteria

required for Commission approval in PURA § 37.056(c)(4); 16 TAC §

25.101(b)(3)(B)?


A. Yes, I did, as follows and as discussed in further detail below:


       (1) Mr. Brewer opines on topics outside of his area of expertise and therefore his

testimony on these topics should not be given weight by the ALJs or the Commission;

                                                 on Behalf of the G6 Landowners Legal Fund LLC

        (2) His most aggressive ecological claim of a confirmed golden-cheeked warbler

breeding pair on the G52 link is not supported by any evidence and the effect of his

claim, if accepted, would be to disfavor a "super majority" in his words, or 70% of all

routes, including his own recommended Route 572;


       (3) His "best meets" route analysis is unsupported by any explanation of the

mathematical basis for the analysis and he failed to produce the results that would allow

the ALJs, the Commission, or parties to the proceeding to evaluate and verify the

accuracy of the analysis and its results;

       (4) He failed to conduct or at least produce any sensitivity analysis to support his

methodology;

       (5) Regarding the G6 and N4 portions of the corridor, Mr. Brewer provided neither

an analysis against the same criteria nor a link-by-link analysis of Route 572

(AO-Al-A2-Bl-B21-C4-D12-C5-E52-Fl-F31-F32-F20-F23-G72-G73-G82-G13-G2-G6-I

l-J31-J32-J33-K41-K42-M31-M32-M33-M4-N4-03-P2-Rl -Tl -T2-Z2); and


       (6) He failed to address the moderation standard doctrinally essentially

attempting to require the Commission to adopt the route with the absolute lowest

aggregate impact, based on his methodology rather than a balanced multi-criteria

standard under 16 TAC § 25.101(b)(3)(B).

Q. In your expert opinion, did you identify flaws or omissions in the analysis

provided by Mr. Smitherman in his direct testimony that are relevant to the criteria

 required for Commission approval in PURA § 37.056(c)(4); 16 TAC §

25.101(b)(3)(B)?


A. Yes. I have identified several flaws and omissions in his analysis that are material to

the Commission's routing determination under PURA §37.056(c)(4) and 16 TAC

§25.101(b)(3)(B).


   (1) First, Mr. Smitherman's routing exclusions, opposing Links G51, G52, J22, J24,

       J26, and N3, do not eliminate all viable routes, but they do eliminate all

       well-performing ones. I reviewed the official link composition of every application

       route from Table 7-1, Appendix D of the Environmental Assessment. Exactly 26

       of the 122 application routes survive his six-link exclusion. However, based on

       my analysis, not one of those 26 routes ranks in the top 16 of all 123 routes

       evaluated under the statutory criteria. The best survivor is Route 296, a G6

       corridor route, at Rank #18. Every route that performs better, including Route 894

       at Rank #1, uses at least one link Mr. Smitherman would have the Commission

       reject. His surviving G6 routes range from Rank #18 to Rank #113; his surviving

       G4 routes range from Rank #61 to Rank #123. The practical effect of his

       exclusions is to remove from consideration every route that best meets the

       statutory criteria.

   (2) Second, the precedent Mr. Smitherman cites most favorably Docket No. 38354,

       the Kerrville/I-10 case, actually supports approval of Route 894. In that case, the

       Commission approved a route with a higher habitable structure count and higher
                                                      Cross-Rebuttal Testimony of Ryan Hopkins
                                                 on Behalf of the G6 Landowners Legal Fund LLC
                                                    regarding Brewer and Smitherman Testimony
                                                                  on behalf of Save the Lampasas
                                                                          PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                  SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                      Page 9 of 38
        cost because it followed an existing corridor. Route 894 achieves corridor

       integrity the lowest habitable structure count of any route in this dataset, and a

       competitive total project cost. His own precedent, applied to these facts, is

       consistent with approving Route 894.

   (3) Third, Mr. Smitherman's concern about Post Oak Ridge State Park is legitimate

       but link-specific; it applies to Links J22 and J26, which Route 894 does not use.

       Route 894 traverses zero parks and has zero park adjacencies, fully addressing

       the community value he identifies.

   (4) Finally, Mr. Smitherman does not identify any route or corridor he would find

       acceptable, even from among the 26 routes his exclusions leave available. The

       Commission is therefore left without affirmative routing guidance from his

       testimony I will address each of these points in turn, below.


Q. Have you conducted an affirmative analysis to identify which routes best meet

the statutory criteria?

A. Yes. Because Mr. Brewer on behalf of Save the Lampasas and Ms. Reinecke on

behalf of CCP have both proposed G6-based routes as affirmative recommendations, I

conducted an independent composite scoring analysis of 123 routes using the

Applicants' own filed data. That analysis identifies 894 as the top-ranked route of all 123

evaluated. The model I present here incorporates an expanded and more granular

weighting structure, built category by category from the statute itself and the public

record in this proceeding. When the statutory weights are applied correctly and

                                                                  on behalf of Save the Lampasas

 transparently the applicants' own proposed route, Route 894, emerges as the

top-ranked route of all 123 routes followed closely by Routes 495 and 488.


            CROSS-REBUTTAL OF MR. BREWER'S TESTIMONY FOR STL

Q. Did you review the direct testimony of Aaron Brewer, RG., Managing Director,

Natural Resources, ESE Partners (Austin, TX) on behalf of STL?

A. Yes, I did.


Q. For the record, how is Mr. Brewer's testimony designated in the PUC

Interchange filing system?


A. It was filed as PUC Interchange Item No. 4494.

Q. Did his testimony include exhibits to support his testimony?


A. Yes.

Q. Did you review those exhibits as part of your review and analysis of his

testimony?

A. Yes, I did.


Q. Based on your review of Mr. Brewer's testimony and exhibits, how would you

summarize the objective of his testimony?

A. Mr. Brewer recommends that the Commission move the line off Link N3 and onto

Link N12 "or N4," and recommends Route 572 as the "best meets" route, while

 identifying additional alternative Routes 295 and 296. His recommended route and the

two alternative routes he suggests all utilize the G6 and N4 links.

Q. Based on your review and analysis of Mr. Brewer's testimony and the exhibits

included with his testimony, did you identify any flaws or omissions in his

analysis that are relevant to the criteria required for Commission approval in

PURA § 37.056(c)(4); 16 TAC § 25.101(b)(3)(B)?


A. Yes, I did.


Q. Is there an issue that affects the weight that should be given to Mr. Brewer's

testimony by the ALJs and the Commission?

A. Yes, Mr. Brewer is not a transmission engineer, a routing consultant, or a wildlife

biologist, and he is not licensed in any field that gives him independent authority over

engineering design, viewshed analysis, FAA obstruction clearance, or ESA habitat

determinations. He is an environmental consultant and natural-resources permitter

rendering an opinion on a route study he did not conduct.

In addition, his most aggressive ecological claim of a confirmed golden-cheeked warbler

breeding pair on the G52 link is sourced to "a bird surveyor hired by a ranch on Link

G52," but the bird surveyor is not identified, his/her survey protocol is not disclosed, and

his/her report is not attached as an exhibit. (Brewer Testimony at p. 6, In 6-8; p. 8, In

1-4; p.23, In 14-16). According to Mr. Brewer, 70% of the 1,246 EA routes use Links

G51 (Brewer Testimony, at p. 23, In 18-21). His unsubstantiated GCWA claim therefore

 would disfavor a "super majority" of routes, in his words. (/d.) Mr. Brewer acknowledged

in his own testimony that the entire project corridor passes through core GCWA

breeding range (Brewer Testimony, p. 23, In 9-10). Yet he conducted no GCWA survey

of the G6 corridor. His GCWA argument, if taken at face value, disqualifies his own

recommended Route 572 as much as it disqualifies Route 894. This logical

inconsistency fatally undermines his ESA-based recommendation of a G6 route.

Further, Mr. Brewer asserts the 140-ft minimum structure height violates 50:1 and 25:1

FAA horizontal-slope standards near unregistered airfields. (Brewer Testimony at p. 17,

In 6-11). He cites no FAA regulation, no FAR Part 77 surface calculation, and no

engineering analysis. As a RG. in Soil Science, this is outside his licensed competence.

Q. Did you identify any flaws in Mr. Brewer's methodology that he used to identify

his proposed "best meets" route?

A. Yes. He stated that he used the evaluation criteria identified in the EA to conduct a

numerical analysis of the 1,246 routes, and for the 122 filed routes that also have

associated estimated construction costs, to identify the route or routes that best meet

the evaluation criteria. (Brewer Testimony at p.21, In 9-17; p. 26, In 14-17). However, he

never provided the mathematical formulas used in his numerical analysis, nor did he

produce the results that would allow the ALJs, the Commission, or parties to the

proceeding to evaluate and verify the accuracy of the analysis and its results. By

contrast, my composite scoring analysis, presented in the Affirmative Route Analysis

 section of this testimony discloses all variables, all weights, the direction of scoring for

each variable, the normalization methodology and the full ranked results for 123 routes.

Every input originates from the Applicants' own filed data.


Further, he indicated that within the Land Use criteria, he applied a special elevated

weight to habitable structures but he did not disclose the actual weight multiplier.

(Brewer Testimony at p. 24, In 7-8).


He removed four of the 35 EA criteria for "zero or near-zero variance" without identifying

them or defining "near-zero." (Brewer Testimony, at p. 21, In 20-21).


He did not indicate that he had conducted any sensitivity analysis. He apparently

developed one composite-score ranking, although that was not provided and cannot be

confirmed. There is no indication that any alternative weighting system was tested. If

habitable structures dropped from "highest weight" within the land use criteria to an

equal weighting, Route 894's ranking within the second percentile for habitable-structure

performance would be improved.

In addition, Mr. Brewer provided no analysis of G6 or N4 against the same criteria. He

performed no foreground-zone analysis, no Angell-Land-and-Cattle-style middleground

analysis, no slope analysis, no stream-crossing inventory no FAA review, and no review

of cultural resources. No link-by-link analysis of Route 572 is provided in the G6 or N4

portion of the corridor. The parcel-level map books filed with my direct testimony (21

sheets of GIS-documented FEMA floodplain crossings, NWI wetland features, habitable

 structure setback violations, uncased water wells, and engineering access constraints)

are the only parcel-level analysis of the G6 corridor in the record.

He does not address the moderation standard doctrinally. He paraphrases 16 TAC §

25.101(b)(3)(B) but does not quote it and does not cite any Commission decision

interpreting the moderation standard. He treats it as if the Commission is required to

adopt the route with the absolute lowest aggregate impact, but this is not the rule or the

        CROSS-REBUTTAL OF MR. SMITHERMAN'S TESTIMONY FOR STL

Q. Did you review the direct testimony of Barry T. Smitherman on behalf of STL?

A. Yes, I did. Mr. Smitherman's testimony was filed as PUC Interchange Item No. 4339.

Q. How would you summarize the objective of Mr. Smitherman's testimony?

A. Mr. Smitherman's testimony has two primary objectives. The first is procedural: to

urge the Commission to slow down, conduct further study and defer a final routing

decision, pointing to unresolved questions about need, changed circumstances since

the ERCOT reliability study and the pending transmission cost allocation proceeding as

reasons to wait. The second is substantive: to eliminate, through his six-link exclusion,

every route that performs well under the statutory criteria, leaving the Commission with

a pool of routes that are concentrated in the bottom half of any balanced statutory

analysis.


                                                      Cross-Rebuttal Testimony of Ryan Hopkins
                                                 on Behalf of the G6 Landowners Legal Fund LLC
                                                    regarding Brewer and Smitherman Testimony
                                                                  on behalf of Save the Lampasas
                                                                          PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                  SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                     Page 15 of 38
 The concerns he raises about private property land stewardship, and the character of

the Hill Country are genuinely important, and the Commission should take them

seriously. But those values are already embedded in the statutory criteria. They are

precisely what PURA §37.056(c)(4) directs the Commission to weigh. When that

weighing is done carefully and transparently using the Applicants' own data, Route 894

is the route that best honors those values.

Q. Did you identify any issues with Mr. Smitherman's analysis?

A. Yes. Mr. Smitherman does not present a quantitative routing analysis, he presents a

legal and policy framework, a set of link exclusions, and a recommendation for further

study The issues I identify are less about analytical errors in a technical sense and

more about what his framework omits and what it produces when applied to this record.

The most significant issue is that his link exclusions are presented without any

demonstration that they are grounded in the statutory criteria. He opposes G51, G52,

J22, J24, J26, and N3, but he does not show, variable by variable, that routes using

those links perform worse under PURA §37.056(c)(4) than routes that avoid them.

When that comparison is actually made using the Applicants' own data, the opposite is

true: routes using G51 dominate the top of the statutory ranking, and the routes that

survive his exclusions cluster in the bottom half.


The second issue is his treatment of habitable structures. Mr. Smitherman correctly

notes that a raw structure count is not a complete proxy for community impact, and I

 agree with that as a general principle. But he uses that observation selectively to

discount the habitable structure advantage of routes he opposes without applying the

same skepticism to the metrics that favor his clients' preferred corridor. A balanced

analysis would scrutinize all variables with equal rigor, not only those that cut against

the recommended route.

Beyond those two points, my concerns are less about what Mr. Smitherman got wrong

and more about what he chose not to address, particularly the absence of any

affirmative route recommendation.

In short: Mr. Smitherman's six-link exclusion functions as a precision instrument to

remove the top 16 routes from the Commission's consideration and replace them with a

set of routes that score between Rank #18 and Rank #123. That is not a routing

recommendation that serves the public interest.


Q. Does the fact that 26 routes survive Mr. Smitherman's exclusions suggest the

Commission still has meaningful options?

A. No, and the breakdown of those 26 routes makes that clear. Eighteen of the 26

survivors are G6 corridor routes. Under the statutory criteria, with appropriate weight

given to habitable structures and total project cost, G6 routes are structurally

disadvantaged: they run through more populated territory and carry higher infrastructure

and aviation conflicts. The best G6 survivor, Route 296, ranks #18 in my analysis, but it

still has 105 habitable structures compared to Route 894's count of 85, while also

costing more. Every G6 route that survives Mr. Smitherman's exclusions performs
